A single layer of low cuboidal cells with no mucin.

Sources

Educational only, not medical advice. Schematic, not to scale: the duct cross-sections, cell counts and positions are illustrative, not measured. The stages show the typical order, not an obligate one: most PanINs never progress, and real tumours vary. On a phone, tap a stage number to step through; hover or focus a duct or a bar for a short explanation. PanIN (pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia) is the main microscopic precursor of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA). Low-grade PanIN is formerly PanIN-1A/1B/2; high-grade is formerly PanIN-3.

  • Stages and histology. Normal duct, acinar-to-ductal metaplasia, low- and high-grade PanIN and invasive PDA, and the two-tier PanIN grading: Basturk O et al., A Revised Classification System and Recommendations for Pancreatic Intraepithelial Neoplasia and Intraductal Lesions, Am J Surg Pathol 2015;39:1730-41 (PMID 26559377); Hruban RH et al., Pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia: a new nomenclature, Am J Surg Pathol 2001;25:579-86 (PMID 11342768); Kumar V, Abbas AK, Aster JC, Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th ed., 2015, ch. 19.
  • Genetic drivers and their order. KRAS (codon 12) from the earliest PanIN (also reported in ADM), CDKN2A/p16 at intermediate grade, then TP53 and, later, SMAD4: as reviewed in Kleeff J et al., Pancreatic cancer, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2016;2:16022 (doi:10.1038/nrdp.2016.22). Frequencies in PDA: KRAS ~90-95%, CDKN2A ~90-95% inactivated (deletion, mutation or methylation), TP53 ~70-75%, SMAD4 ~55% (Robbins 9th ed. ch. 19; Hahn SA et al., Science 1996;271:350-3 for SMAD4). SMAD4 is lost in about a third of high-grade PanIN, most often at invasion: Wilentz RE et al., Cancer Res 2000;60:2002-6. KRAS prevalence in low-grade PanIN is assay-dependent: older assays found 36-44%, sensitive sequencing over 90%.
  • Ki-67 proliferation index by grade (dividing cells bar). Klein WM et al., Direct correlation between proliferative activity and dysplasia in pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PanIN), Mod Pathol 2002;15:441-7 (PMID 11950919): normal 0.41%, PanIN-1A 0.69%, 1B 2.33%, grade 2 14.08%, grade 3 22.01%, invasive carcinoma 36.99%.

Left out / simplified: sub-grades within low-grade PanIN, BRCA2 and other hits, GNAS (an IPMN driver, not PanIN), the acinar vs ductal cell-of-origin debate, and the difference between the human sequence shown here and the compressed course seen in mouse models.
